content.title: COOKING MISTAKES THAT QUIETLY {{DRAIN}} YOUR NUTRIENTS
facts: **Broccoli** – Boiling it lets much of its **vitamin C** leach into the water; a few minutes of steaming keeps most of it intact.
**Tomatoes** – Refrigerating them slows the ripening process that increases usable **lycopene**, so counter storage is often the better choice.
**Onions** – Rinsing them after chopping washes away some of the beneficial sulfur compounds that give them their heart-supportive properties.
**Spinach** – Cooking it in reactive metal pans can cause it to lose more of its **iron** than cooking in stainless steel or glass.
**Lentils** – Many assume red meat is the main source of **iron**, but a cooked serving of lentils delivers a comparable amount without the saturated fat.
**Bell Peppers** – Ounce for ounce, red bell peppers often edge out oranges in **vitamin C**, yet the nutrient-rich white pith usually ends up in the trash.
